title: China Readies for a Record Number of Humanoids - The Wire China
gist: China's humanoid robot makers are racing to manufacture tens of thousands of units this year even though demand is lagging far behind: leaders Unitree and AgiBot together sold fewer than 11,000 humanoids last year, a supply-versus-demand gap the article frames as the sector's real bottleneck.

insights.claim: China's humanoid robot manufacturers are racing to build tens of thousands of machines this year, but the article frames finding enough buyers as the harder challenge than production itself.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A production-ahead-of-demand dynamic in Chinese humanoid robotics is a red flag for oversupply and price competition in the sector — investors should watch order books and inventory, not just manufacturing capacity announcements.
insights.quote: China's humanoid robot makers are racing to build tens of thousands of machines this year. The harder task will be finding enough customers to buy them.

insights.claim: China's two leading humanoid robot firms, Unitree and AgiBot, combined sold fewer than 11,000 humanoids last year, about 10,000 more units than in 2024, but this remains far behind the deployment scale of other (non-humanoid) robot types in China.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Sub-11,000-unit combined annual sales from the two market leaders is a concrete, low base for a sector often discussed in terms of speculative future scale — useful benchmark for sizing near-term humanoid robot revenue versus industrial robotics.
insights.quote: China’s two leading robot firms, Unitree and AgiBot, combined sold fewer than 11,000 humanoids last year — about ten thousand more than 2024 but still far behind deployment of other types of robots.
insights.locator: China’s two leading robot firms, Unitree and AgiBot

insights.claim: China has already deployed hundreds of thousands of non-human industrial robots, showing that humanoid robot adoption is lagging well behind the country's broader industrial automation base.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The large existing base of non-humanoid industrial robots versus the tiny humanoid installed base suggests near-term automation capex in China is still flowing overwhelmingly to conventional industrial robots, not humanoids.
insights.quote: While China has already deployed hundreds of thousands of non-human industrial robots, humanoid sales are lagging.
insights.locator: While China has already deployed hundreds of thousands
